title: India set to install additional 200 million air conditioners by 2035: IEA
description:
India is set to install an additional 200 million air conditioners in homes over the next decade, making it the biggest driver of global energy demand growth, the International Energy Agency said in its World Energy Outlook 2026.
The agency said India and Southeast Asia's share of the global stock of air conditioners (ACs) will rise from "less than 10 per cent today to 20 per cent by 2035". In India and Indonesia, the IEA said, "fewer than one in five households own an AC, despite high cooling needs".
By comparison, around 90 per cent of households in Australia, Japan and the United States own at least one AC.
The IEA said "for the first time in energy history", demand for cooling in buildings is overtaking demand for heating.
India's electricity demand is likely to grow 6 per cent a year, over the next decade, under the IEA's Stated Policies Scenario, the fastest of any major region. Total energy demand is expected to rise 2.5 per cent annually, "triple the global rate".
